thread:
alex: thinking we need a new synth generator that focuses on tail shaping, but also makes apples-to-apples comparisons with replay harnesses. goal: reproduce p95/p99 regressions caused by batching+kernel selection changes.

sam: +1. what shape are you thinking? pure bursts or mixed patterns?

alex: mixed. a baseline Poisson arrival for steady qps, plus configurable burst windows (size, duration, inter-arrival within burst). also support heavy-tailed session lengths so KV cache hit rate varies by client.

katie: suggest we add an MMPP mode (markov-modulated Poisson) so bursts are correlated over time. that matches production where some customers send sustained spikes.

nate: for kernel selection tests we should parameterize sequence-length distribution too. short vs long tokens changes fused vs unfused kernel choice. small change in seq-dist -> different kernel -> p99 blip.

priya: agree. also add a "warmup phase" option for KV prefix caching: e.g. fill prefixes for X seconds, then start measured traffic. otherwise tail skew is dominated by cold-cache misses.

alex: rough CLI prototype:
```
run_synth --mode=mmpp --base-qps=200 --burst-config='size:400,duration:12s,interval:3m' --seq-dist=zipf(1.2) --kv-warmup=30s --seed=42
```
keep logs simple so we can compare runs.

sam: nice. what metrics we store? p50/p95/p99, batch size histogram, kernel-choice counts, kv-hit-rate by client bucket, cpu/gpu utilization, latency breakdown (queue vs compute vs io).

perf-bot: nightly-run summary: kernel-selector-rollout A/B saw p99 +15% on small-batch-heavy workload. nvprof traces point to more kernel-switch overhead at sequence boundary. link: https://perf.corp/reports/180509_kernswitch

katie: that perf-bot note is key. generator should be able to create "sequence boundary" events (requests that jump from short->long) to trigger the kernel switch overhead. maybe a toggle to insert boundary requests every Nth session.

nate: for apples-to-apples compare: same model weights, same tokenization, deterministic seeds, and run with and without the batching heuristic. collect per-token cost and per-token latency. then compute delta on p99.

priya: we should also add a JSON output for each run with these fields: config, aggregate metrics, per-client kv hit histogram, kernel-breakdown. that makes diffing easy.

alex: action items: katie will draft MMPP + boundary toggle by EOD Wed, nate will add seq-dist profiles and kernel counters, priya will add kv-warmup and per-client histograms. sam and i will wire up the CLI and JSON output. i'll open a draft PR and link here. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created issue PERF-814 for synth-gen work (assign: katie,nate,priya,alex).

sam: one more thought — include a "replay-mode" that consumes captured production arrival timestamps but normalizes client distribution so we can do apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic.

alex: perfect. that'll let us validate synthetic modes against real traces. thanks everyone.
